notes.text: This leaf states a theorem identifying two categories: data (tilde X-star, dotted X, E, Y, f), with a germ of cylindrical neighbourhood, and data (X,Y,T), with a germ of conical neighbourhood. The marginal note proposes an analogue using strict tubular neighbourhood structures rather than germs and says 'à voir !' (the à remains uncertain). It restricts the morphisms to isomorphisms in the clause beginning 'morphismes ici sont les isos, pour simplifier'; the terminal mark is now a doubtful closing parenthesis/exclamation mark. No separate Les precedes morphismes in the native margin context. The theorem is reported faithfully, not certified by this transcription.

The display is literally X = tilde X-star amalg_{dotted X} Y. The lower NB then discusses subsets with equal inverse images and their closedness, before an incomplete compatibility criterion beginning a). The page ends at the short form 'au vois.'; no continuation, missing condition, equals sign, accent or star is supplied from a later leaf.

Targeted set-theoretic proof of the subset correspondence. Write S=tilde X-star, B=dotted X, i:B→S for the inclusion, and q:S disjoint-union Y→X for the quotient generated by i(b)~f(b). For D⊂X, put A=q_S^{-1}(D), C=q_Y^{-1}(D). Then i^{-1}(A)=f^{-1}(C), since related generators have the same image. Conversely, assume this equality for A⊂S,C⊂Y. The indicator of A disjoint-union C has equal values on every generating pair i(b),f(b); equality propagates along every finite chain generating the equivalence relation. Thus A disjoint-union C is saturated, q^{-1}(q(A disjoint-union C))=A disjoint-union C. D=q(A disjoint-union C) is therefore the unique subset with these inverse images. This verifies precisely the source's matching-inverse-images statement for the displayed quotient; it does not use a collar, local triviality, compactness or separation.

Targeted topological proof of the closedness assertion. For the matched pair in N03, the quotient topology gives D closed in X iff q^{-1}(D) is closed in S disjoint-union Y (apply the definition to complements). A subset of a disjoint topological sum is closed iff its restrictions to both summands are closed. Hence D is closed iff A is closed in S and C is closed in Y. Saturation, proved in N03, is essential when starting from A,C. No claim that arbitrary images of closed sets under q are closed is used.

A further limited check of the stated gluing construction uses the hypotheses that B is closed in S and f is continuous. Because i is an inclusion, the generated equivalence relation does not identify two distinct points of the Y summand, so j=q_Y:Y→X is injective. If D⊂Y is closed, f^{-1}(D) is closed in B and therefore in S, and q^{-1}(j(D))=i(f^{-1}(D)) disjoint-union D is closed. By quotient topology j(D) is closed in X. Since j is continuous, it is a closed embedding. Also q restricts to a homeomorphism S\B→X\j(Y): it is bijective there, and any relatively open U⊂S\B is open in S because B is closed; q^{-1}(q(U))=U, so q(U) is open in X. This checks the closed-subspace component of target data b), not the germ correspondence, fullness, faithfulness or essential surjectivity of the asserted equivalence.

Literal notation is not repaired by the proofs. In 'partie tilde X-prime-star de X-star' the second X-star has no tilde, although the displayed quotient uses S=tilde X-star. The later compatibility line uses tilde X-prime and the pair (tilde X,dotted X) without stars. The final parenthesis writes X-star=tilde X\dotted X. These may reflect changes of notation or slips, but the assigned leaf does not determine a consistent replacement. N03–N05 explicitly use the displayed pushout interpretation and do not silently rewrite these prose formulas.

The source writes 'Pour que X′ soit compatibles' with a plural s and later 'fermé' before ssi; both literal endings remain. The final annotation tilde X-prime_1 stands above-left of the closure bar over X-prime intersection X-star, with no equals sign. The ambient space of that closure and the unfinished next assertion are not independently specified here, so no proof of the full compatibility criterion or completion assertion is claimed.

Present unreadable ink is explicitly retained: the independent upper-right mass in the tuple is represented by the empty-content mathematical doubt, with its location and unestablished state stated in the TeX comment. No certain previous glyph is supplied under the overworked folio, dotted X body, initial Une, or germe. The second audit adds a possible dotted-T underlayer beneath dotted X as an explicitly uncertain alternative. The dense equivalence-like sign in the upper margin has a preferred cancelled state but remains doubtful; the following word équivalentes is independent ink.

Reading record: the full original and the two supplied native halves were each inspected once, then all 23 stable saved crops were visually read. An early four-image tool response was truncated before any of P01–P04 was delivered to the reader; those four files were subsequently displayed singly for their actual first inspection. There was no OCR, external research, compilation, other-page access, or new crop of a decided place. line_count=22 counts the principal main-text baselines including the central display, excluding folia, raised replacements and the separately inventoried margins. No genuine diagram or drawing occurs on this leaf.

Collation metadata: an empty c or h string with the corresponding omission flag records that the witness does not represent the targeted ink; it is not a proposed empty source reading. Every final excerpt and every audit first reading is checked as a whitespace-normalized substring of the comment-stripped draft. C/H fragments are checked against their assigned-page files. These are textual consistency checks, not a TeX compilation or an additional image reading.

Independent audit: root inspected all eighteen nonidentical boxes and a wider native context of the upper diagonal note. Thirteen boxes were revised, predominantly to record local uncertainty while retaining the preferred reading. The lower marginal clause no longer contains the unsupported initial Les; its final curved mark now prefers a closing parenthesis with an exclamation-mark alternative. The headless connector, literal equals shorthand and completer lexeme were retained. The fixed first and second readings remain unchanged; these visual decisions are not additional mathematical proof events.

audit_changes.evidence: The upper-right ascending stroke and rounded lower return support 6. A darker tall stroke also survives at its left, but cannot be separated confidently from overtracing. Six remains preferred, with 16 retained as a possible segmentation rather than an asserted earlier digit.

The tall d and dotted i support Considérons, but the opening is crossed by the diagonal marginal writing and several low joins are not independently visible. The same word is retained with local uncertainty; Thm, its underline and les remain clear.

The first crossed group consists mainly of low connected loops; the second has the conspicuous tall paired uprights of définies. Ainsi définies remains preferred. The second reader’s ci-après définies is a possible segmentation of the first group under the strike and is added as an alternative; C’s reverse order is retained at lower confidence.

The small initial a) lies directly in the crossing of the oblique note and the main baseline. The closing curve survives, but the letter body cannot be isolated completely. The category label a) is retained as a local doubt; the cancelled noun and raised systèmes retain their existing readings.
